name: Keyu Zhu
headline: People analytics · Psychology · Data visualisation
short_bio: I’m Keyu Zhu (Colby), an MSc student in People Analytics and Human-Centric Management at UCL. My background in psychology informs my interests in human behaviour, research and data visualisation.
about: I studied Psychology at the University of Warwick before joining UCL’s School of Management. My research experience spans attention and emotion, decision-making and language learning, and donor mental health. Internships in user research and public affairs have also given me experience working with feedback, content and audience data.

education.qualification: MSc People Analytics and Human-Centric Management

research.title: Instruction Effects on the Attentional Blink for Negative Words
research.summary: Investigated whether emotion-focused instructions affected the identification of negative words during the attentional blink.
details: Designed a 2 × 2 rapid serial visual presentation experiment, manipulating instruction type and target lag.
Implemented the experiment in PsychoPy and Pavlovia; measured second-target accuracy conditional on correct first-target identification (T2 | T1).
Evaluated the implications for emotional processing and attentional control.

research.title: Impact of Distinction Bias on Decision and Language Learning
research.summary: Examined how comparisons between options can influence artificial-vocabulary learning.
details: Collected more than 150 questionnaire responses using picture-matching tasks, spelling and multiple-choice questions.
Used Python for data cleaning and SPSS for statistical analysis.
Considered how decision-making bias mechanisms apply to learning contexts.

research.title: Psychological Health Scale for Liver Donors
research.summary: Contributed to research on the mental health of voluntary liver donors.
details: Worked with the Beck Scale for Suicide Ideation (BSS) and Meaning in Life Questionnaire (MLQ).
Investigated the relationship between recipient recovery and donor psychological wellbeing through hospital fieldwork.

research.title: Analysis of Smartphone Addiction Today: A Literature Review
research.summary: Contributed to a team literature review on smartphone addiction.
details: Independently compiled chapters on four treatment intervention programmes and research conclusions and prospects.
